brand.statementNote: This is our mission, not a promise about any particular sidewalk. Conditions change — always use your own judgement.

meta.description: PathAble helps people who use wheelchairs, scooters, walkers, canes and strollers compare pedestrian routes by known sidewalk conditions, barriers and community reports. Toronto pilot in development.

how.title: Built around how you move — not an average pedestrian.

profile.title: Tell us what matters
profile.body: Choose a starting profile — or none — and adjust slope, stairs, curb ramps and surface preferences. You can change them any time.

compare.title: Compare honest routes
compare.body: See each option's known barriers, unverified reports, missing data and how fresh the information is — side by side, in words and on the map.

go.title: Go with clear directions
go.body: Large-text, step-by-step directions with optional voice guidance. Every map detail has a text alternative.

report.title: Report what you find
report.body: Snap a photo of a barrier. AI can suggest what it sees; you confirm or correct it before anything is shared.

profiles.title: Starting points, never assumptions.
profiles.body: Profiles pre-fill sensible preferences. Every setting stays yours to change, and you never have to tell us why.

states.title: Four kinds of knowledge. Never blurred together.
states.body: Most maps treat “no data” as “fine”. PathAble shows exactly what is known, what is reported, and what nobody has checked yet.
states.explore: Select a state to highlight it in the illustration.

verified.title: Known accessible
verified.body: A trusted source has checked this stretch against your preferences: slope, width, surface, curb ramps.

barrier.title: Known barrier
barrier.body: A verified obstacle, such as stairs or a missing curb ramp. Routes that avoid it rank higher if it conflicts with your profile.

reported.title: Reported, not yet verified
reported.body: Someone in the community flagged a problem. We show it with its age and number of confirmations until it's verified or expires.

unknown.title: Missing information
unknown.body: Nobody has surveyed this section yet. It is never presented as accessible — it lowers a route's confidence instead.

ai.title: The model suggests. People decide.
ai.body: Upload a photo and a computer-vision model can point out curb ramps, obstructions and damaged surfaces it thinks it sees. You review every suggestion, correct mistakes, and only then submit.
ai.point1: Every suggestion shows the model's confidence.
ai.point2: Your corrections are kept with the report and help improve future versions.
ai.point3: If the model isn't available, reporting still works — you just describe it yourself.
ai.status: The analysis service is not connected in this preview.

community.title: Local knowledge, carefully handled.
community.body: Reports start as unverified, show how many people confirmed them, and expire when conditions are temporary. You can withdraw or correct your own reports at any time.

winter.title: A cleared road isn't a cleared sidewalk.
winter.body: Snowbanks over curb ramps, ice on a slope, a windrow at the crossing. Winter reports get their own markers, timestamps and short expiry times — because conditions change overnight.
winter.weatherNote: Weather forecasts are never shown as sidewalk conditions. Only on-the-ground reports are.

trust.title: We'd rather say “we don't know” than guess.

safe.title: No “100% safe” routes
safe.body: We describe what is known. We never promise a route is safe or fully accessible.

sources.title: Every fact has a source and a date
sources.body: Municipal open data, field surveys, community reports or model assistance — always labelled, always timestamped.

explain.title: Recommendations come with reasons
explain.body: When one route is suggested over another, we tell you why in plain language.

correct.title: You can correct us
correct.body: Spot something wrong? Report it. Corrections are part of the product, not an afterthought.

inclusive.title: Accessibility isn't a feature. It's the foundation.
inclusive.body: PathAble is built toward WCAG 2.2 AA, tested with keyboards and screen readers, and set in Atkinson Hyperlegible — a typeface designed for low-vision readers.

items.keyboard: Full keyboard access, including the map
items.languages: English and French today; 10 more languages in progress

availability.title: Starting in Toronto. Built for Canada.
availability.body: PathAble is in active development. The interface you see is real; the routing and analysis services are being built. Toronto is our first planned coverage area.

coverage.areaBody: The City of Toronto, with address search across the Greater Toronto Area. Expansion to other Canadian cities will follow once the data and verification processes are proven here.
coverage.dataBody: Municipal open data (such as sidewalk inventories), field surveys, OpenStreetMap, and community reports. Each item on the map will show which source it came from and when it was last observed.
coverage.notBody: PathAble is not an emergency service, doesn't replace orientation and mobility training, and can't guarantee any route's condition.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.lede: Accessibility is PathAble's purpose, so we hold ourselves to a high standard — and we're explicit about what's been tested.
accessibility.targetBody: PathAble is built to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA. We have not yet had an independent audit, so we don't claim conformance.

done.semantic: Semantic HTML landmarks, headings and form labels
done.keyboard: Every control works with a keyboard, with a visible focus outline
done.map: Every map detail is also available as text: route summaries, sections, hazards and directions
done.color: Status is never shown by colour alone — lines have patterns and every state has a label and icon
done.contrast: Colour tokens are checked against WCAG contrast ratios in our build pipeline
done.motion: Animations respect reduced-motion settings, with an in-app override
done.text: Text can be scaled to 150% without loss of content
done.touch: Touch targets are at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels
done.announce: Route results and changes are announced to screen readers

accessibility.testingBody: Automated checks run axe-core on every page in our end-to-end test suite, alongside keyboard-only interaction tests. Manual testing guidance for screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, TalkBack) is documented in the project repository.

known.map: The map canvas itself is visual; we provide equivalent information in the panel rather than describing the canvas.
known.translation: Only English and French are available while other translations are completed and reviewed.
known.audit: No independent audit or testing with disabled participants has been completed yet.

accessibility.feedbackTitle: Tell us about barriers in PathAble itself
accessibility.feedbackBody: If anything in PathAble is hard to use with your setup, please let us know through the contact page.

help.title: Help centre
help.lede: Answers about routes, data, reporting and privacy.

safe.q: Does PathAble guarantee a route is accessible?
safe.a: No. PathAble shows what is known about a route — verified conditions, known barriers, unverified reports and missing information — and ranks options using your preferences. Conditions change, so always use your own judgement.

unknown.q: What does “no data” mean on a route?
unknown.a: Nobody has surveyed that section yet. We never treat missing information as accessible. Routes with more unknown sections rank lower when you prefer verified routes.

sample.q: Why does the app say “sample data”?
sample.a: The routing service is still being built. Until it's connected, routes and hazards are generated samples so the interface can be tested. They don't follow real sidewalks and must not be used to navigate.

profile.q: Do I have to tell PathAble about my disability?
profile.a: No. Profiles are optional shortcuts that pre-fill preferences. You can skip them, use Custom, and change any setting. Preferences are stored on your device.

ai.q: How is AI used in reporting?
ai.a: When available, a computer-vision model suggests what barriers might be in your photo, with a confidence level. You confirm or reject each suggestion. Nothing is reported without your review.

winter.q: Do you use weather forecasts to predict snow on sidewalks?
winter.a: No. Weather isn't sidewalk condition. Winter markers only come from on-the-ground reports, and they expire quickly.

photos.a: Location metadata in the file is removed before upload. Photos are only sent when you submit a report, and the planned service will blur faces and licence plates. In this preview, reports stay on your device.

keyboard.q: Can I use PathAble without a mouse or touchscreen?
keyboard.a: Yes. Everything works with a keyboard. Press {shortcut} anywhere to search actions, and use Tab to move between route options. The map can be panned with arrow keys once focused.

languages.a: English and French today. Spanish, Arabic, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Hindi, Urdu, Bengali, Punjabi, Tamil and Portuguese will be added once each translation is complete and reviewed.

data.a: Yes. Settings → Privacy & data lets you download or delete everything PathAble stores on your device.

contact.title: Contact & support
contact.lede: PathAble is an early-stage project. Here's how to reach the people building it.
contact.issuesTitle: Report a problem or suggest an idea
contact.issuesBody: Bugs, accessibility issues and feature ideas are tracked publicly.
contact.noChannel: A public support channel hasn't been set up for this deployment yet.
contact.responseBody: There's no staffed support line or guaranteed response time yet. For anything urgent or safety-related, contact local services — PathAble is not an emergency service.
contact.barrierTitle: Found a barrier on a sidewalk?
contact.barrierBody: Use the report flow so it can be shown to others.
contact.cityBody: PathAble doesn't repair sidewalks. In Toronto, you can report sidewalk and snow-clearing problems to the City through 311.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: Plain-language overview of how PathAble handles data in this preview.
privacy.draftNotice: This page describes the preview's behaviour and the intended structure of a future privacy policy. It is not a legal policy and has not been reviewed by a lawyer.

device.title: Stored on your device
device.body: Preferences, display settings, onboarding status and saved reports are kept in your browser's local storage. They don't leave your device unless you send a report once the service is live.

location.title: Location
location.body: Your location is requested only when you choose “Use my location”. It's used to set a starting point or report location and isn't stored by PathAble in this preview.

search.title: Address search
search.body: What you type into search is sent to the geocoding service (Photon, operated by Komoot, using OpenStreetMap data) to find matching places.

map.title: Map tiles
map.body: Map images are loaded from OpenFreeMap. Like any web request, this reveals your IP address and the map area you view to that provider.

photos.title: Photos
photos.body: Photos stay on your device until you submit a report. Location metadata is stripped before upload.

analytics.title: Analytics and tracking
analytics.body: This preview contains no analytics, advertising or tracking scripts.

rights.title: Your choices
rights.body: You can download or delete everything PathAble stores on your device from Settings at any time.

future.title: Before launch
future.body: A full privacy policy covering accounts, report storage, retention periods and your rights under Canadian privacy law (PIPEDA) will be published before any personal data is collected on a server.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lede: The intended structure of PathAble's terms, shared early for transparency.
terms.draftNotice: Draft structure only — not a binding agreement and not legal advice.

preview.title: Preview software
preview.body: PathAble is in development. Route information in this preview is sample data and must not be used for real-world navigation.

judgement.title: Use your own judgement
judgement.body: Route information can be incomplete or out of date. PathAble doesn't guarantee that any route is safe, accessible or passable.

reports.title: Community reports
reports.body: Reports should describe real conditions, avoid identifying people, and not include harmful or misleading content.

data.title: Map and data attribution
data.body: Map data is © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License. Other sources are credited where they appear.

ai.title: How PathAble uses AI
ai.lede: Where AI is used, where it isn't, and the limits we design around.
ai.usedTitle: Where AI is planned to be used

used.photos: Suggesting barrier types and locations in photos you submit.
used.triage: Helping reviewers prioritize reports that may affect many routes.

not.routing: Deciding on its own whether a sidewalk is accessible. Model-assisted information is always labelled and reviewed by a person.
not.profiles: Inferring anything about you from your preferences or behaviour.

limits.accuracy: Models make mistakes, especially in snow, low light, or with unusual infrastructure.
limits.bias: Training images may under-represent some neighbourhoods or seasons. We plan to measure accuracy by area and season and publish the results.
limits.confidence: Confidence scores are estimates, not guarantees.

ai.statusBody: No AI model is connected. The reporting flow shows an “unavailable” state instead of inventing results.
